body:
## Feature Summary

A scheduled task that runs outside the coordinator session, with no model in the loop, performs the coordinator's periodic read-only checks, compares them with the last recorded state, and wakes or pings the coordinator session only when something actually changed or a decision is outstanding for the first time.

## Problem Statement

The standing coordinator session keeps a recurring cron prompt that fires every 10 minutes; each firing runs the session's sweep and report pass even when nothing changed, printing "Nothing has changed, and nothing new needs you..." into the channel every tick. This fills the channel with noise and spends model tokens on every tick for zero information. WC-16 makes the coordinator run the sweep itself at most once every 5 minutes on every wake or wait timeout (src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md:290) and states "Phase 1 adds this duty, not a scheduler", so today there is no scheduler outside the session to suppress the empty ticks.

## User Story

As the project owner, I want the periodic checks to run in a model-free scheduled task that wakes the coordinator session only when there is something to act on, so that the channel stays quiet and tokens are not spent on unchanged ticks.

## Proposed Solution

The goal: move the read-only observation duty (the collection and classification that `superclaude sweep run` already performs read-only, src/superclaude/cli/sweep/commands.py:242-288) into a scheduled task outside the coordinator session. That task compares each run's result with the last persisted state and, only on a real change or a first-time outstanding decision, wakes the coordinator session through an existing wake channel (Orca messages, `orca terminal send` as used at src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md:136, or a cross-session SendMessage). Constraints:

- The scheduled task must remain read-only in effect apart from its own state file and report output (the sweep package already keeps exactly one writing function, `_publish`, src/superclaude/cli/sweep/commands.py:153-208).
- WC-16's rules stay authoritative: only Orca's stall proofs make a worker stalled; the sweep recommends nothing (src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md:290).
- The coordinator's wait (`orca orchestration check --wait ... --timeout-ms 300000`, src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md:102) and its re-arm behaviour must stay compatible with being woken by the outside task.
- The cron entry pattern already exists in the issue watcher (`src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/dispatch.py`, one cron entry running a sweep with absolute paths) and can be the model for a cron-driven coordinator wake path.

The concrete design (scheduler choice, state comparison format, wake channel, and the WC-16 wording change) is to be produced by a `/sc:brainstorm --depth deep` session; this issue does not fix it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With no changes between two consecutive scheduled checks, the coordinator session produces no per-tick report output (no "Nothing has changed..." message) and no model tokens are spent on the tick.
- [ ] When a real change occurs (worker result, new message, first-time outstanding decision), the outside task wakes the coordinator session and the coordinator handles it under the existing WC-6/WC-16 rules.
- [ ] The scheduled task itself performs only read-only checks apart from its own state and report files.
- [ ] WC-16 and "Liveness supervision" in src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md are updated to describe the new division of duty.

## Out of Scope

- Changing what the sweep classifies or probes (the sweep package's read model stays as is).
- Removing the coordinator's in-session re-arm of its Orca wait (src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md:290, "When a wait on Orca expires, the coordinator re-arms it").
- The issue watcher's own cron loop (separate feature, #450).

## Components Affected (from `/sc:analyze`)

- src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md:96-108 ("Liveness supervision", the `--wait` call) and :288-290 (WC-16, coordinator loop, "Phase 1 adds this duty, not a scheduler").
- src/superclaude/cli/sweep/ (commands.py, probes.py, classify.py, models.py, report.py): the existing read-only sweep the scheduled task would reuse.
- src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/dispatch.py:1-10,451 — existing cron-entry pattern (one cron entry, absolute paths, flock skip of overlapping ticks) to model the outside scheduler.
- src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/scripts/orca_worktree.py:890 — existing CronCreate allowlist entry (a wake-up scheduling tool reference already allowlisted there).

## Related Issues/PRs

- #716 (coordinator follow-ups from the 655 gap list — same coordinator loop area)
- #717 (issue watcher follow-ups; separate scheduled component)
- #755 (coordinator created multiple Orca Runs; same coordinator scheduling area)
- #751 (issue watcher retry; same watcher/cron family)
- #450 (issue watcher cron roll-out; the cron pattern this feature would reuse)
- #706 (observer follow-ups: sweep source and scale tests)
- #725 (coordinator asks peer coordinator before a human; coordinator loop behaviour)

## Priority

Medium: degraded behaviour with a workaround (the coordinator still runs and the owner can read the channel past the noise) plus a planned feature (the outside scheduler WC-16 explicitly does not add yet); the trigger is the every-10-minute empty report the description names.

## Fix approach

Repo: IronbellyOrg/IronClaude. Base branch: master.

Commands, in order: /sc:brainstorm --depth deep (in a separate session, to propose the ideal design), then /sc:design or /sc:workflow, then /sc:implement, then /sc:pr-submit --monitor 3.

Steps, in order:

- Step 1: Run `/sc:brainstorm --depth deep` in a separate session over this issue to choose the design: scheduler (cron entry vs CronCreate), state-comparison format, and the wake channel (Orca message, `orca terminal send`, cross-session SendMessage). Inputs: src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md (WC-16, "Liveness supervision"), src/superclaude/cli/sweep/, src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/dispatch.py.
- Step 2: Capture the chosen design as a spec/plan with `/sc:design` or `/sc:workflow` (the follow-on command the brainstorm handoff names), including the WC-16 wording change.
- Step 3: `/sc:implement` the plan: the outside scheduled check (state file, compare, wake call), the WC-16/"Liveness supervision" contract update in src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md, and tests alongside tests/sweep/.
- Step 4: `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3` to open the PR against master on IronbellyOrg/IronClaude.

## Test plan

Assumptions stated in the section: the outside task reuses the sweep package's collectors (src/superclaude/cli/sweep/probes.py) rather than adding new probes, and its state file lives under `.dev/` like the sweep reports (src/superclaude/cli/sweep/commands.py:101-103).

- Tests to add or change: extend tests/sweep/ (pattern of tests/sweep/test_readonly.py and test_cli_contract.py) with tests for (1) an unchanged second observation produces no wake and no coordinator-facing output, (2) a changed observation or first-time outstanding decision produces exactly one wake call, (3) the scheduled task's writes are confined to its state file and `.dev/` report output.
- Regression gate: `uv run pytest tests/sweep/` then the full `make test`, `make lint`, and `make verify-sync` (WORKER-CONTRACT.md is a synced core file).
- How a reviewer verifies: run `uv run pytest tests/sweep/ -v` and confirm the new tests pass; `make verify-sync` passes after the WORKER-CONTRACT.md edit; manually create the cron entry in a scratch checkout, let two ticks pass with no changes, and confirm the coordinator channel stays silent, then change a watched input and confirm one wake.

<!-- sc:issue:create template=issue-feature-simple -->



## Brainstorm result (2026-11-24, deep brainstorm, nothing built)

Recommended next step: **/sc:workflow** (the design is chosen, so what remains is a multi-file plan, not an architecture dialogue). Five owner decisions and one live test must come before any build. Local files: `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/recommendation.md` and `merged-requirements.md` (same folder; local paths, not committed).


Status: the design is complete and debated. It is not ready to build until the owner answers five questions (section 4) and one live test passes. No live Orca call, no commit and no GitHub action was made.

Full design brief: `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/merged-requirements.md` (replacement contract text is in its section "Contract wording"). Debate record: `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/nested/adversarial-1/adversarial/`.

## 1. The recommended design

**What runs outside the session, and where.**
- A new command, `superclaude coord-watch tick`, run by the system cron daemon every 5 minutes. No model is involved. Cron is running on this host (checked with `pgrep` and `crontab -l`). `CronCreate` is rejected because it is a model-run, session-only scheduler.
- The cron line uses absolute paths, sets `ORCA_CLI_COMMAND` to the shim the issue watcher already uses under cron (`/home/coder/.config/orca/linux-orca-cli-shim/orca`), and runs `flock -n <root>/.dev/sweeps/watch/cron.lock timeout -k 5s 120s superclaude coord-watch tick --root <root>`. The tick takes its own second lock, `state.lock`, on a different file. One shared file would make every tick skip itself.
- The new code is a new package, `src/superclaude/cli/coord_watch/`, next to the sweep package. It imports the sweep's collectors, classifier and JSON builder. It never calls `_publish`, so it writes no report and the sweep package still has exactly one writer and 10 read-only Orca commands (`probes.py:49-60`). A wake is an Orca write, so it cannot live in the sweep package.

**How state is compared and stored.**
- State file: `<root>/.dev/sweeps/watch/state.json`. That folder is gitignored (`.gitignore:256`), so the file never shows up in the sweep's own git reading. Writes go to a temp file, then fsync, then `os.replace`. A state file that is unreadable, has an unknown field, names another root, is a symlink or is over 4 MiB is renamed `state.bad-<time>` and the tick starts a fresh baseline, so nothing needs manual repair.
- The comparison is a hash of the facts that matter: per row its class, waiting kind, rule and policy; Orca and source health; worktree frozen state and packages; and the contract fields (path, worker status, question, reason, command). Left out because they change every tick or on every worker edit: timestamps, ages, evidence text, notes, and the dirty and unpushed flags.
- A first-time outstanding decision is keyed `<row>|<waiting kind>|<rule>`. A key is forgotten only after the row has been out of the waiting class for 2 ticks, so one bad read does not wake twice. A move into or out of "could not determine" wakes only after 2 ticks.
- The first tick records a baseline silently and wakes only if a decision is already waiting.

**How the coordinator is woken.**
- One Orca mailbox message: `orca orchestration send --to run:<id> --type status --subject "[coord-watch] ..." --payload {source, version, run, event_id, ...}`. `status` is already in the coordinator's wait types (`WORKER-CONTRACT.md:102`). The body names only the row, the class change and the waiting kind. It never holds a path, the word "complete" or worker text, because a status that names a report path sets S9 (`WORKER-CONTRACT.md:109`).
- `orca terminal send` and `SendMessage` are rejected: typing needs an idle-prompt judgment cron cannot make (`WORKER-CONTRACT.md:136-138`), and `SendMessage` is a model tool.
- Delivery is at least once. The saved baseline moves only after the send exits 0. A failed send keeps a pending event with a stable `event_id` and retries it first on the next tick. The coordinator skips an `event_id` it already recorded as swept.
- The coordinator tells the watcher which Run to watch with `superclaude coord-watch set-run <id>` right after each bind. A new binding re-baselines the watcher. The Run id is not put in the crontab, because Runs change (#755).

**What changes in the contract (WC-16, `WORKER-CONTRACT.md:290`, and "Liveness supervision").**
- Remove "Phase 1 adds this duty, not a scheduler". Say that the cron-run watcher sends the wake.
- `/sc:sweep` runs only on a `[coord-watch]` wake, on any message other than `heartbeat`, or on a wait timeout while the watcher is unhealthy. A healthy empty timeout and a heartbeat-only wake run nothing and print nothing.
- A wake that arrives inside the 5-minute cap is deferred, not dropped: the run-notes line says `deferred <event_id>` before the ack, and `swept <event_id>` after the pass.
- The watcher is healthy only if its Run matches, its last tick is at most 15 minutes old, its last outcome is `unchanged`, `woke` or `rebased`, and no pending event is older than about 300 seconds. `coord-watch status --run <id>` returns that as exit 0 or 1.
- Line 109 gets a rule, placed before the ack and S9 clauses, that recognizes a valid `[coord-watch]` status and never treats it as an ack, a completion or a stall proof. "The sweep." (line 111) stays in the session unchanged. `docs/designs/orchestrator-mode.md:686` repeats the old sentence and needs the same edit.
- The three phrases pinned at `tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py:171-173` stay.

## 2. Main risks and how each is handled

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| The idle coordinator still costs model turns: about 12 silent wait timeouts an hour plus one per heartbeat batch (`WORKER-CONTRACT.md:102,111`) | The PR says so plainly. Out of scope: the issue keeps the in-session re-arm. A 3600000 ms idle wait is a follow-up that must state a failure-detection bound. |
| The owner's recurring 10-minute in-session prompt keeps printing "Nothing has changed". It lives in the owner's memory, outside the repo | Owner decision 3. Without it, acceptance criterion 1 is not met. |
| The owner's own wait command leaves out `status`, so a wake would sit unread up to an hour | Owner decision 2. The contract wait at line 102 already includes `status`. |
| A hand-added crontab line is lost: the crontab blocks say "managed: rewritten on every boot" | Install through the managed (Coder template) path, or as a gated step in the issue-watch dispatcher that does not hold its lock for 120 seconds. Owner decision 1. |
| A watcher that looks fresh but fails every send | The closed health rule above, checked at each timeout. |
| Coordinator rebinds to a new Run and the watcher stays silent | `set-run` writes a new generation, which re-baselines. A Run mismatch without a new generation counts as unhealthy. |
| A wake is swallowed by the 5-minute cap | Deferred, not dropped, with `deferred` and `swept` notes. |
| Orca is down, rows vanish and old decisions wake again later | With Orca down the tick does not compare, keeps the baseline and records `orca_down`. |
| A second writer creeps into the sweep package | Boundary tests: AST scan, the pinned 10-command allowlist, one writing module and one process start in the new package. |

## 3. What I could not verify (UNVERIFIED)

- UNVERIFIED: that `orchestration send --to run:<id>` from cron, with no terminal and no Run binding, is accepted and wakes the coordinator's `check --wait`. Every variant depends on it. The send help only says "a sender in no Run must use run:<id>".
- UNVERIFIED: that `check --wait` returns at once when an unacked delivery is already waiting.
- UNVERIFIED: that `orca-ide`, which the sweep probes call by default, reaches the Orca runtime from cron, or that the shim works for the sweep's read commands. The issue watcher uses the shim from cron; nothing was run through it for this brief.
- UNVERIFIED: that `git` is on the PATH of the line that gets installed, and which socket or authentication environment a headless send needs.
- UNVERIFIED: that the model follows the new contract text (the health check, deferred and swept). A live test samples it once; nothing enforces it.
- UNVERIFIED: that `CronCreate` is session-only with a 30-day expiry (the repo only holds the allowlist string at `orca_worktree.py:890`); the exact text of the current 10-minute prompt; that Orca accepts `--timeout-ms 3600000` (seen only in the owner's memory).
- UNVERIFIED: the 4 MiB limit, the 300 s pending age and the 120 s outer timeout are starting values. The names `coord-watch`, `set-run` and `watch/` are proposals.
- Not settled by the debate: whether a change that is only "quiet" moves the baseline (INV-003), and one Run per watcher when a coordinator owns several (INV-021).
- Protocol notes: the brainstorm skill file gives 350K tokens per proposal for a deep run and its agent-spec reference gives 35K. The skill file's figure would refuse every deep run, so I used the reference's. Also, the reference writes agent instructions in single quotes while the adversarial skill says double quotes. I treated single quotes as quoted.

## 4. Open owner decisions (none was decided here)

1. Install path: the managed crontab template, or a gated step in the issue-watch dispatcher.
2. Replace the owner's wait command in memory with the line-102 wait.
3. Retire the in-session recurring prompt, or narrow it to `ListAgents`, the PR check and `notify_when_idle`. Only retiring it meets criterion 1 as written.
4. Accept the idle cost above, or order the follow-up that moves liveness reads outside the session.
5. Authorize one live headless send from cron to a scratch Run, plus the deferred-then-swept check, before any build.

## 5. Best next step: `/sc:workflow @.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/merged-requirements.md`

- The design and the replacement contract text are already chosen, so the remaining work is a multi-file implementation plan with checks, not a dialogue about architecture, which is what `/sc:design` is for.
- The plan should start with the live send test (decision 5) and the install path (decision 1), and hold the contract edit until decisions 2 and 3 are answered.
- Ask the owner the five questions in chat first. The plan can be written before the answers, but it cannot be built.

## Backlog review, 2026-11-24

Read-only review of this issue against the current source and its history (automated analysis, then an independent evidence review that passed).

- **State:** in-progress
- **Complexity / size:** Complex / L
- **Priority:** P2

#### Concrete next steps
1. Preserve the completed research rather than restart the brainstorm. Reconcile the live issue and initial risk plan with the latest recorded answers before commissioning an implementation plan. The earlier eleven-minute watcher and uniformly three-minute wait are superseded: `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/risk-tests/DECISIONS-2.md:7-23` records a stamp-gated 25-minute watcher, a three-minute wait while busy, and a 45-minute wait while idle. Managed Coder installation and a narrowed recurring prompt were recorded earlier in `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/risk-tests/PLAN.md:9-13`. Original chat authority for both rounds remains **UNVERIFIED** here; this audit does not grant approval. The later record still leaves the narrowed prompt interval open at lines 37-41.
2. Revise the existing design before implementation: include cron sender identity, receive `status` messages, account for incomplete worker coverage, and carry forward the corrected fingerprint. For the latest cadence, the later research derives a 55-minute health limit, not the earlier 25-minute limit; that is a derived recommendation, not a separately verified owner choice. Its saved three-seed simulation gives worst detection delays of 58 minutes busy and 100 minutes idle: `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/risk-tests/DECISIONS-2.md:15-23` and `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/risk-tests/raw/t3b-runs.jsonl:1-3`. The coordinator must reconcile these latency bounds with the intended supervision requirements before planning rollout. Do not declare every prior risk test passed: the spaced fingerprint acceptance check failed and its correction was checked offline only, per `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/risk-tests/results.md:43-51,108-113`.
3. Make a checked implementation plan from the revised requirements, keeping the read-only sweep separate from the write that wakes the coordinator. Cover saved-state recovery, duplicate wake handling, retries, Run changes, quiet unchanged ticks, fallback when the watcher fails, and deferred wakes within the existing observation cap. Preserve coordinator re-arm and existing stall-proof rules. Source boundaries: `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Issuecleanup/src/superclaude/cli/sweep/probes.py:49-60` and `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Issuecleanup/src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md:104-115,288-290`.
4. Implement and validate only after the coordinator establishes the needed grants. Tests must cover unchanged silence/no model call from the scheduled checker, one first-time decision wake, retries and corrupted state, incomplete observations and delivery into the coordinator's actual wait. Update the contract and its matching design text, and arrange managed installation outside this repository. No install, live experiment or source change is authorized by this review.
5. Keep acceptance criterion 1 scoped explicitly: a model-free checker does not make the retained in-session wait or narrowed model prompt token-free. Require measured savings and a real coordinator-handling check; both remain **UNVERIFIED** by this audit. Prior findings already distinguish delivery from model behaviour: `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/risk-tests/results.md:82-113`.

#### Dependencies
- No hard issue-number prerequisite or downstream blocked issue is established by the live issue; do not invent a dependency edge from a related-issues list.
- #755 (OPEN, coordinator Run creation and switching rules) is an integration dependency to settle or explicitly account for before deployment, not proof that all work must wait for its closure: a watcher bound to the wrong Run can miss work. `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/merged-requirements.md:250` explicitly leaves older Runs unwatched after a rebind.
- Managed scheduler installation belongs to the Coder template according to `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/risk-tests/PLAN.md:9`. A concrete Coder issue number and its completion are **UNVERIFIED** here; this review is restricted to IronClaude GitHub reads.
- #450 (CLOSED, issue watcher rollout) and #751 (CLOSED, failed-first-run retry) are existing cron/reliability precedent, not open blockers. #716, #717, #706 and #725 overlap the coordinator ecosystem but no strict requires/blocks relationship was verified.

#### Related issues
Live titles and states were checked on IronbellyOrg/IronClaude:
- #716, OPEN: coordinator next-release features from issue 655; wider coordinator scope, not a duplicate of change-only scheduling.
- #717, OPEN: issue watcher features from issue 655; separate watcher.
- #755, OPEN: coordinator creates multiple Runs; directly relevant to watcher Run binding.
- #751, CLOSED: issue watcher never retries a failed first run; retry precedent, not this feature.
- #450, CLOSED: issue watcher rollout, live test, shadow run and cron; scheduling precedent.
- #706, OPEN: observer follow-up including sweep source and scale tests; relevant to observation coverage.
- #725, OPEN: coordinators ask peer coordinators before humans; decision-routing overlap.
These are related by the live issue's explicit list and their verified titles/states; this report does not assert all their acceptance criteria have been satisfied.

#### Related PRs
No implementation PR is linked or numbered in issue #757's current body or comments. Read-only PR searches across all states for `757`, `coord-watch` and `coordinator sweep` found no relevant implementation PR. The `757` search returned merged PR #508 (commit `146be6fc34276c99d4bff89e682472274f71ce8e`), but its body says 757 tests passed; it is a numeric false match and does not implement this issue. No relevant PR number can be supplied without inventing one. Differently named or unpushed work elsewhere is **UNVERIFIED**.

The required architecture command completed; report: `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Issuecleanup/.dev/issuecleanup/g6/757/analyze/analyze-report.md`. This audit ran no tests, no Python/UV command, no cron change, no live wake and no GitHub write; prior experiment results above are read from disk only.

_Limits: the full GitHub event timeline could not be read in this review and is unverified. Nothing was changed on this issue other than this comment and its field values._

If we scanned the session logs for any file updated in the last x minutes, mapped session logs to session ID or whatever other metadata the coordinator needed, when the scan found files changed, it sent the coordinator a ping to follow up on those session.

title: [FEATURE] Run the coordinator sweep outside the session and wake it only on change
